public_brief: Our vending firmware team wants the transaction session modeled before anyone touches hardware. Implement vend_step(state, event, amount_cents=0, credit_cents=0, price_cents=0) as a pure reducer and return a tuple (next_state, credit_cents). The session state is one of the strings idle, collecting, exact_change, dispensing; events are the strings coin, select, refund. amount_cents is the value of the coin being inserted (leave 0 for the other events), credit_cents is the credit already sitting in the session, and price_cents is the price of the one product this machine sells. Graders call the function directly with ordinary purchase flows and with adversarial ones - odd amounts, every event fired in every state, junk states and events - and compare the returned tuples, so every combination needs a defined answer. Pure function: no printing, no I/O, no exceptions.
entry_contract: Implement vend_step(state, event, amount_cents=0, credit_cents=0, price_cents=0) taking two strings then three ints as positional arguments and returning a (state_string, credit_int) tuple for every input combination.

hidden_spec.rule: A coin with a positive multiple-of-5 amount adds amount_cents to the credit; the first coin from idle moves the session to collecting, and in collecting (or exact_change) further coins keep stacking with no cap.
The coin slot only accepts positive multiples of 5: an amount of zero, negative, or not a multiple of 5 is ignored entirely - same state, same credit.
select in collecting with credit_cents at or above price_cents vends: it returns ("dispensing", 0) - the machine keeps the price and the leftover credit goes back as change.
select when the credit is below price_cents returns its inputs unchanged - no vend, no error - whatever the state.

In exact_change, a coin that would push the credit above price_cents is refused unchanged (the machine cannot make change); coins that keep the credit at or below the price are accepted and the session stays exact_change.
In exact_change, select vends only on an exact match - credit_cents equal to price_cents returns ("dispensing", 0); a credit above the price is refused unchanged.
refund from collecting or exact_change returns ("idle", 0); refund from idle is a no-op that also returns ("idle", 0).
dispensing is terminal - every event there returns ("dispensing", 0) - and any unknown state or event name returns its inputs unchanged without raising.

answer_sheet.answer: Every good coin stacks onto the credit with no cap. The first coin from idle wakes the session into collecting, and in exact_change the coins keep stacking too - dropping money in doesn't reset the mode.
The slot only takes positive multiples of five - nickels on up. Pennies, odd-value slugs, zero, and negatives are ignored outright: same state, same credit, no complaint.
Select with credit at or over the price vends: state goes to dispensing and the credit zeroes out - the machine keeps the price and hands the rest back as change.
Select with credit under the price does nothing at all - same state, same credit. No error, no partial vend, it just sits there.

In exact_change a coin that would push credit over the price is refused - the change hopper is empty and we can't make change. Coins that keep it at or under the price go through, and the session stays in exact_change.
Exact-change mode vends only on a perfect match: credit equals price, you get dispensing and zero. Credit over the price is refused - we'd owe change we can't give.
Refund wipes the session: back to idle with zero credit, from collecting or exact_change alike. From idle it's a harmless no-op - idle, zero.
dispensing is the end of the line - any event there returns dispensing, zero. And unknown states or events hand back exactly what came in; nothing ever throws.
Out of scope - this machine sells one fixed-price product; stock counts and spiral assignments are the stocker's problem.
Out of scope - no jam sensors or diagnostics here; the reducer only sees clean events.

provenance.derivation: Rules derived from real vending-machine conventions (nickel-multiple coin mechanisms that reject pennies, uncapped credit accumulation, dispense-and-return-change, exact-change-only mode that refuses overpayment, coin-return reset, vend as a terminal state), not from any WiseCounsil design document.
